questions.question: A sum invested at the rate of 6% simple interest per annum grows to Rs. 1,13,880 in 5 years. What is the simple interest, If the same amount is invested for 8 years at the rate of 9% per annum?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Final amount after 5 years = Rs. 1,13,880

Rate of interest for first investment = 6% per annum

Time period for first investment = 5 years

Rate of interest for second investment = 9% per annum

Time period for second investment = 8 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × Time / 100

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P.

Amount after 5 years at 6% per annum = P + (P × 6 × 5 / 100)

⇒ 1,13,880 = P + (P × 30 / 100)

⇒ 1,13,880 = P + (3P / 10)

⇒ 1,13,880 = (10P + 3P) / 10

⇒ 1,13,880 = 13P / 10

⇒ P = 1,13,880 × 10 / 13

⇒ P = Rs. 87,600

Now, calculating simple interest for 8 years at 9% per annum:

Simple Interest = 87,600 × 9 × 8 / 100

⇒ Simple Interest = 87,600 × 72 / 100

⇒ Simple Interest = Rs. 63,072

**Therefore, the simple interest for 8 years at 9% per annum is Rs. 63,072.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest (in Rs.) on Rs. 20,500 for 2 years at 10% per annum, if the interest is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹20,500

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Concept Used:**

Compound Interest Calculation

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)T

Compound Interest (CI) = A - P

**Calculation:**

A = 20,500 × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 20,500 × (1 + 0.10)²

⇒ A = 20,500 × (1.10)²

⇒ A = 20,500 × 1.21

⇒ A = 24,805

Compound Interest = Amount - Principal

⇒ CI = 24,805 - 20,500

⇒ CI = 4,305

**∴ The compound interest is ₹4,305**

questions.question: What will be the compound interest (in ₹) on ₹ 10,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum, compounded annually?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 10,000

Rate = 5%

Time = 2 years

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T

CI = A – P

**Calculation:**

According to the question

A = P(1 + R/100)T

⇒ A = 10,000 × (1 + 5/100)²

⇒ 10,000 × (105/100)²

⇒ (10,000 × 21/20 × 21/20)

⇒ (25 × 21 × 21)

⇒ Rs.11,025

Now,

CI = A – P

⇒ CI = Rs. (11,025 – 10,000)

⇒ Rs. 1025

**∴ The required CI is Rs. 1025**

questions.question: The compound interest on Rs. 60000 at 4% per annum is Rs. 4896. What is the time period in years?
questions.solution:

The rate of percentage = 4%

The compound interest = Rs. 4896

**Formula used:**

{CI}= {P × [(1+{Rover100})^T - 1]} Where, SI = Simple interest, CI = Compound interest, P = Principle, R = Rate, and T = Time

**Calculation:**

Let the time be T

⇒ {4896}= {60000 × [(1+{4over100})^T - 1]}

⇒ {4896over60000}+1 = {(1+{4over100})^T }

⇒ {64896over 60000} = {(1+{4over100})^T }

⇒ {10816over 10000} = ({104over100})^T

⇒ ({104over100})²=({104over100})^T

⇒ T = 2 

**∴ The required result will be 2 years.**

questions.question: A farmer borrowed ₹1,32,000 from a money lender to do cultivation in his field. The rate of interest is 12.5% p.a. compounded annually. At the end of two years, he cleared his loan by paying ₹1,07,062.50 and his scooter. The cost (in ₹) of the scooter is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal(P) = Rs. 132000

Rate of interest(r) = 12.5%

Time(t) = 2 years

He paid Rs. 107062.5 and his scooter

**Concept used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

**Calculation:**

12.5% = 1/8

So,

Amount = 132000 × 9/8 × 9/8

⇒ 167062.5

So,

Price of the scooter = 167062.5 - 107062.5 = 60000

**∴ The cost (in ₹) of the scooter is 60000**
